svg.title: Densities under a linear map, and the tails of three source priors
svg.desc: Left: the uniform density on zero to one has height one. Doubling the variable spreads it over zero to two, and the density halves to keep area one; plugging x over two into the original density without the determinant factor gives height one over a width of two, area two. Right: log densities of unit-variance Gaussian, logistic and Laplace distributions. The Gaussian falls as a parabola; the logistic and Laplace fall linearly, so far from zero they are orders of magnitude more likely.
